sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned Tribunal has not awarded sufficient compensation and compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Hence, appropriate compensation be awarded and it be suitable enhanced.
3. Learned counsel for the Insurance company submits that compensation awarded by Tribunal is just and proper.
Hence, no enhancement is required.
Therefore, appeal filed by the appellant be dismissed.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

5. As per para 26 of the impugned award, learned Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs.31,696/- for expenses during treatment and Rs.10,000/- under Mental and physical pain, nourishing diet and attendant charges; total Rs.41,696/-.

6. After perusal of record, it appears that amount Rs.10,000/- awarded under Mental and physical pain, nourishing diet and attendant charges, is found to be on lower side, however, considering the nature and facts of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to enhance the compensation amount awarded by learned Claims Tribunal by Rs.20,000/- in lump sum which shall be payable to appellant/claimant in addition to already awarded amount under the aforesaid head by the claims tribunal i.e. Rs.10,000/-.
7.

Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand only)
which appellant/claimant will be entitled to in addition to the amount awarded by learned Claims Tribunal.
This additional amount will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the Claim Petition, till the date of its actual payment.
All other conditions of the award shall remain intact.
8. Appeal is partly allowed to the aforesaid extent and disposed of.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE shahina Pradeep Kumar Vishwakarma vs Abhisekh Singh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148355874/
